purpose: Native-speaker validation set for Nigerian Pidgin output. This is what the Pidgin support claim rests on: we claim it because a speaker checked it, not because NLLB emitted something Pidgin-shaped.
instructions_for_reviewer: The 'draft' field is a FIRST ATTEMPT written by the model, not by a speaker. Treat it as something to correct, not something to approve. Correcting is faster than composing from nothing, but a wrong draft you leave alone becomes a wrong reference.
Rewrite each draft the way you would ACTUALLY say it to a farmer. Naija as it is really spoken, not English with a few words changed.
Set 'draft_ok' to yes or no. If no, put your version in 'corrected'.
Items marked CRITICAL are safety messages. If those do not land as urgent and clear, the safety design fails at the last step - a farmer who does not understand a warning is not warned.
If the ENGLISH itself would confuse a farmer, say so in notes. Bad English in, bad Pidgin out.
Leave anything you are unsure about blank rather than guessing.
why_pidgin_matters: Nigerian Pidgin has the widest reach of any language in this project - it crosses ethnic lines in a way Yoruba, Hausa and Igbo do not, and it is what many farmers actually use at market. It is also the language most likely to be mistaken for 'informal English' and translated carelessly.

review.method_note: The reviewer read the full draft set and approved it as a whole, rather than marking each row individually. This is genuine native-speaker validation and is recorded as such, but it is weaker evidence than per-row correction: a blanket pass cannot distinguish a line that is right from one the reviewer skimmed. Stated plainly here so REPORT.md can describe the basis of the African-language claim accurately rather than implying line-by-line verification.
